title: Seal the Foundation context manifest record
description: Prerequisite for task-203a5ca7aada4375a98a95df8773e249; hard-depend on task-c7f2530b4a4445398a5e572f0568ea1d. @moe/context's manifest digest binds its seven render fields and exactBytes, but not project/session/node/attempt/graph/config/input provenance and it has no durable decoder. Define the daemon-owned canonical authority envelope and strict codec without changing the context package.
definitionOfDone: One exact versioned FoundationContextManifestRecord binds projectId, sessionId, nodeKey, attemptRef, graphRevisionRef, graphContentHash, graphEpoch, configurationDigest, inputManifestDigest, the complete public ContextRenderManifest, and an outer recordDigest over every field; all ids/digests/integers/keys are bounded and deeply frozen.

The encoder accepts only descriptor-safe exact-key plain data, requires manifest.version `context-manifest.v1`, byte values 0..255 and nonempty exactBytes, recomputes `digestContextManifest(manifest.binding)`, and derives rather than trusts recordDigest.

The decoder uses bounded canonical bytes, distinguishes exact MALFORMED, VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH, RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH and NONCANONICAL codes at a frozen FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_CODEC layer, re-encodes and byte-compares before returning authority.

Focused tests pin the complete code/key/version roster, hostile accessors/proxies/unknown keys/oversize/truncation/negative-zero cases with a positive generated count, one accepted real renderContext control, and mutations hashing a reference or omitting an outer binding field that redden named assertions.
Context and daemon package tests/typecheck execute separately with nonzero counts; completion records the ledger child of task-203a5ca7aada4375a98a95df8773e249 as consumer.
taskRails: Own only apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-context-manifest-codec.ts, its exact one-line LF .js bridge, and its focused test; production source <=250 lines.
Use public @moe/context `digestContextManifest`; never copy its canonical digest, accept a caller digest/reference, or claim its inner digest binds outer authority fields.
No store, launch, registry, graph reader, or provider behavior in this codec task; exact stable code/layer assertions and explicit owned-path commit.

implementationPlan.description: TDD the encoder's admission rules, each as its own arm with its exact code and the `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_CODEC` layer, and each asserting NOTHING is returned as authority. (a) `manifest.version` other than `context-manifest.v1` -> VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, kept separate from MALFORMED because a knowingly-declined real shape and a shape that is not what it claims lead to opposite operator actions. (b) An `exactBytes` entry outside 0..255, a non-integer, or a NEGATIVE ZERO -> MALFORMED. Negative zero is named explicitly in DoD 4 and is the subtle one: `JSON.stringify(-0)` is `"0"`, so a canonical round-trip silently normalises it and a naive equality check never sees the difference — detect it with `Object.is(value, -0)`, and apply the same check to `graphEpoch`. (c) Empty `exactBytes` -> MALFORMED; the render manifest never legitimately carries zero bytes. (d) A `manifest.digest` that does not equal a fresh `digestContextManifest(manifest.binding)` -> MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH. (e) A caller-supplied `recordDigest` that disagrees with the derived one -> RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH; rail 2 forbids accepting a caller digest at all, so the encoder DERIVES and the mismatch is how that is proven rather than asserted.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 — ENCODER ADMISSION ARMS WRITTEN, still RED on module-absent (the correct red; step 5 turns it green). Eleven new cases, each asserting its exact code AND the `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_CODEC` layer.

NO AUTHORITY RIDES ALONG ON A REFUSAL, enforced centrally. Every refusal goes through `refusalOf()`, which asserts `ok === false` and then `expect(result).not.toHaveProperty("record")` and `not.toHaveProperty("bytes")`. That is the step's "assert NOTHING is returned as authority" made structural rather than repeated eleven times by hand — a refusal that quietly carried a half-built record would fail every arm at once.

(a) VERSION — `manifest.version: "context-manifest.v2"` -> `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`, plus an explicit `expect(code).not.toBe("FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MALFORMED")`. The step's reasoning is why that second assertion exists: a knowingly-declined REAL shape and a shape that is not what it claims lead to opposite operator actions, so the two codes must never quietly merge.

(b) BYTE RANGE — a parameterized `it.each` over four entries (256, -1, 12.5, "7") all -> `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MALFORMED`.

NEGATIVE ZERO, the subtle one DoD 4 names, gets its own case AND a proof of why a normal check cannot see it. The test first asserts the trap itself: `JSON.stringify(-0) === "0"`, `-0 === 0` is `true`, `Object.is(-0, 0)` is `false`. So a canonical round-trip normalises `-0` away and every digest over those bytes is byte-identical to the `+0` case — no byte comparison, no digest comparison and no `=== 0` guard can detect it; only `Object.is` can. Covered on BOTH fields the plan names: an `exactBytes` entry and `graphEpoch`.

I ADDED A CASE THE PLAN DID NOT ASK FOR, because without it the two `-0` arms are not trustworthy: "accepts a POSITIVE zero graphEpoch". If the implementation simply rejected zero, both `-0` tests would pass while the guard was wrong — a green suite hiding a rejected legitimate value. Pairing the refusal with the acceptance is what makes the arm specifically about the SIGN rather than about zero (`mem:qa-refusal-only-suite-cannot-see-a-wrong-accepted-value` is the general shape).

(c) EMPTY `exactBytes` -> `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MALFORMED`. Justified by the step-1 measurement that a genuine `renderContext` manifest always carries nonempty bytes, so zero bytes is a malformation and not a legitimate edge.

(d) INNER DIGEST — `manifest.digest` replaced with a plausible 64-hex string that is not `digestContextManifest(binding)` -> `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH`.

(e) OUTER DIGEST — a caller-supplied `recordDigest` of `"f"*64` -> `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, plus a companion asserting that on the ACCEPTED path `result.record.recordDigest` equals the DERIVED value. Together those two are the executable form of rail 2's "never accept a caller digest": one proves disagreement is refused, the other proves what comes back is the derivation rather than the input.

API DECISION, disclosed because it shapes the test surface. The encoder takes all ELEVEN keys including `recordDigest` (exact-key admission), derives the digest itself, and refuses on disagreement — which is what makes arm (e) reachable at all. That means a caller needs a way to produce a well-formed record, so the module also exports `deriveFoundationContextRecordDigest(tenFields)`. The alternative — a ten-key draft input — would make arm (e) unreachable by any honest fixture, since an eleventh key would simply fail the exact-key check as MALFORMED and the RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH code would be dead (`mem:qa-planted-row-reaches-a-guard-no-honest-fixture-can`).

THE CIRCULARITY, NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. `validRecord()` builds its digest with the PRODUCTION deriver, so the acceptance cases are not independent evidence about the digest's contents — they would pass against any self-consistent deriver. That is deliberate and it is the right trade: using a hand-written second implementation would be the tautology this board has flagged before (`mem:tautology-test-both-operands-hand-written`), and it would drift. The real evidence about the digest is step 4's per-field sweep, which compares digests ACROSS different inputs — that comparison is not circular, and step 7's drills (i) and (ii) are what prove it bites.

FIXTURES STAY REAL: every case starts from `realManifest()`, a genuine `selectContext` -> `renderContext` output. `manifestWith()` structurally clones it before varying a field, because `renderContext` returns a deeply frozen manifest that cannot be mutated in place.

implementationPlan.description: TDD the hostile-input sweep and the accepted control. HOSTILE, with a POSITIVE GENERATED COUNT asserted so a sweep that silently produced zero cases cannot pass: accessor (getter) properties on the outer record and on `manifest.binding`, a revoked Proxy, `__proto__` and other unknown keys, a null-prototype object, oversize payloads past the bounded-decode limit, and truncated bytes. Each must refuse with its exact code and layer; none may let a value survive into the returned record. Reuse `exactKeys`, `isRecord` and `snapshotFoundationValue` from `./foundation-attempt-codec.js` — the descriptor-safe helpers already exist in this directory and a second implementation would drift from them. THE ACCEPTED CONTROL, which DoD 4 requires and which a refusal-only suite is blind without: build a REAL `AdmittedContextSelection`, run the REAL `selectContext` then the REAL `renderContext` from the `@moe/context` root, feed the resulting `ContextRenderManifest` into the encoder with plausible outer identities, and assert the encode succeeds and the decode returns a deeply frozen record whose every field round-trips. Do not hand-forge the manifest — the whole point is that a genuine renderContext output is admitted.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 — HOSTILE SWEEP AND ACCEPTED CONTROL WRITTEN, still correctly RED on module-absent.

ELEVEN HOSTILE CASES, and the count is asserted three ways before the sweep runs: `> 0`, exactly `11`, and all names distinct (a duplicated name silently halves a sweep while the length still looks right). Epic rail 6 requires the generated count to be proven nonzero; a sweep that produced zero cases would otherwise pass while testing nothing.
Cases: accessor on the outer record; accessor on `manifest.binding`; revoked Proxy as the record; revoked Proxy as the manifest; an extra unknown key; a MISSING key; a null-prototype record; an array; `null`; a string; and an oversize manifest (1.2M `exactBytes` entries) past the bounded-decode limit. Each asserts the code is a member of the frozen roster, the layer is `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_CODEC`, and no `record` rides along.

EACH CASE IS A LAZY BUILDER, NOT A PREBUILT VALUE — a deliberate choice. A revoked Proxy stored in an array literal can throw when the harness merely inspects the array to build test names, which would turn the sweep into a collection-time crash rather than eleven refusals. Building at call time keeps each input hostile exactly at the moment the encoder sees it (`mem:array-isarray-throws-on-revoked-proxy` is the same family).

I ADDED "a missing key" alongside the extra-key case. `exactKeys` refuses on key-COUNT mismatch first, so an extra key and a missing key travel different paths through the same guard; testing only the extra would leave the under-supplied record unproven.

TWO DECODER-SIDE CASES the encoder sweep cannot reach:
- TRUNCATED bytes (last 3 bytes sliced off) -> `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MALFORMED`.
- NON-CANONICAL bytes -> `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_NONCANONICAL`. The fixture prepends a single SPACE to the canonical JSON: still valid JSON, parses to an identical value, different bytes. That is precisely the input a parse-only decoder accepts and a re-encode-and-compare decoder refuses, so it is the arm that makes step 7's drill (iii) meaningful. Truncation and non-canonicality get DIFFERENT codes because they are different operator situations — damaged transport versus a re-serialised record.

THE ACCEPTED CONTROL, which DoD 4 requires and without which a refusal-only suite is blind to a wrong ACCEPTED value:
- The manifest comes from the REAL `selectContext` -> `renderContext` chain. Nothing hand-forged; the point is that a genuine render output is admitted.
- All NINE outer identities are asserted individually after the round trip, not as one `toEqual` on the whole record — a whole-object comparison passes even when a field was dropped and re-added from the same fixture object.
- The COMPLETE public manifest is asserted to survive, field by field: version, digest, ordering, rendererVersion, journalCountLimit, journalTextLimit, exactBytes, exclusions, optionalSelection. DoD 1 says "the complete public ContextRenderManifest", so a summary would be a silent narrowing.
- DEEP freezing is asserted at five levels: record, manifest, binding, exactBytes, exclusions, optionalSelection. `Object.isFrozen` on the top object alone is satisfied by a shallow freeze while the nested arrays stay mutable.
- A third case re-encodes the DECODED record and asserts byte-identity with the original encode. That is the executable statement that the record is its own canonical form, and it is stronger than a digest comparison because it catches an ordering or spelling difference that still digests the same only if the digest were computed over the parsed value rather than the bytes.

HELPERS ARE COMPOSED, NOT REWRITTEN. The production module will use `exactKeys`, `isRecord` and `snapshotFoundationValue` from `./foundation-attempt-codec.js` as the plan requires. I verified in step 1 why those already fail closed on this sweep's inputs: the shared `copyValue` refuses any property descriptor without a `value` slot, which is exactly what makes an accessor and a revoked proxy refuse rather than execute. A second `exactKeys` that admitted an accessor while the original refused it would be a divergence living in durable bytes.

implementationPlan.description: TDD the property that the outer digest binds EVERY outer field, which is the real deliverable and the one DoD 4's mutation clause targets. Write a per-field sweep over the ten non-digest outer fields (projectId, sessionId, nodeKey, attemptRef, graphRevisionRef, graphContentHash, graphEpoch, configurationDigest, inputManifestDigest, manifest): for each, mutate that field alone, re-derive, and assert `recordDigest` CHANGES. Assert the generated case count is exactly 10 and greater than zero. This is what makes "an outer binding field was omitted from the digest" a red test rather than an invisible defect — omitting `graphEpoch` from the hashed input leaves every other assertion green. Separately assert the inner and outer digests are independent: changing an outer identity must NOT change `manifest.digest`, and changing `manifest.binding` must change BOTH. Rail 2 is explicit that the inner digest does not bind outer authority fields, so this pair is the executable form of that rule.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 — THE PER-FIELD DIGEST SWEEP, the central test of this task. Still correctly RED on module-absent.

TEN VARIATIONS, ONE PER NON-DIGEST OUTER FIELD, each moving THAT FIELD ALONE and asserting `recordDigest` changes. Count asserted `> 0` and exactly `10` before the sweep runs.

THE SWEPT SET IS CHECKED AGAINST PRODUCTION'S OWN KEY LIST, which is the assertion I consider most valuable here and which the plan did not ask for: `FIELD_VARIATIONS`' field names, sorted, must equal `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_RECORD_KEYS` minus `recordDigest`. A hardcoded `toBe(10)` alone goes stale the day an eleventh outer field is added — the new field would be unswept and unbound, and every existing arm would stay green. Tying the sweep to the production roster means a new field must either be swept or fail this test immediately.

EACH ARM ASSERTS THE VARIATION ACTUALLY VARIED (`expect(varied[field]).not.toEqual(base[field])`) BEFORE asserting the digest moved. Without that, a fixture whose "different" value happened to equal the base would assert "the digest changed when nothing changed" and fail confusingly, or worse, a typo'd field name would silently test nothing.

THE `manifest` ARM VARIES THROUGH A GENUINELY DIFFERENT RENDER, not through the `null` placeholder in the table — a second real `selectContext` -> `renderContext` over different mandatory content. Varying it to `null` would test that the deriver notices a missing manifest, not that it binds a real one; and a null would also be refused upstream, so it would prove nothing about the digest.

I ADDED A STABILITY ARM the plan did not name, and it is load-bearing: "the same fields derive the same digest twice". Every other arm in this block asserts a digest CHANGED. A deriver that returned a random value per call would satisfy all ten of them while binding absolutely nothing. The stability assertion is what makes the ten difference assertions mean what they appear to mean.

THE INDEPENDENCE PAIR — rail 2 made executable:
- Changing an outer identity (`projectId`, `graphEpoch`) leaves `manifest.digest` UNCHANGED, while the OUTER digest moves. This is the concrete statement that the inner digest binds only its seven render fields and has no opinion about project, session, node, attempt, graph, config or input — measured in step 1 from `ContextDigestBinding`'s seven members.
- Changing `manifest.binding` moves BOTH digests.
Together these forbid the plausible shortcut of reusing `manifest.digest` as the record's identity, which would let two records describing different projects at different epochs share one identity. That is the collision this whole envelope exists to prevent, and it is now a red test rather than a comment.

WHY THIS BLOCK IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: the acceptance cases in step 2 use production's own deriver on both sides and so are not independent evidence about the digest's CONTENTS. This block is, because every assertion compares digests ACROSS DIFFERENT INPUTS — no arm here would pass merely because two copies of the same arithmetic agree. Step 7 drills (i) (hash a reference instead of canonical bytes) and (ii) (omit one outer field) target exactly these arms, and drill (ii) must redden EXACTLY ONE of the ten while the other nine stay green — which is the proof that the sweep is genuinely per-field rather than a single lump assertion wearing ten names.

Rail 1 calls this out and it is invisible to typecheck and vitest, so I checked with Python rather than a shell grep: the file is 56 bytes, `b"\r" in data` is **False**, and its trailing bytes `b'ec.ts";\n'` are byte-identical in shape to the sibling `foundation-attempt-codec.js`. COMPOSED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED, exactly as planned: `exactKeys`, `snapshotFoundationValue`, `encodeFoundationPayload`, `decodeFoundationPayload`, `sameBytes`, `isRecord` all come from `./foundation-attempt-codec.js`. `digestContextManifest` comes from the `@moe/context` ROOT and is recomputed from the caller's own binding, never trusted. No second canonical layer, no local hashing of the inner manifest.

=== THE REAL FINDING OF THIS STEP: THE DECODER COULD NOT RE-ADMIT ITS OWN OUTPUT ===
First run was 6 failures / 44 passes. Rather than loosen an assertion I probed the pipeline and isolated it exactly:
```
exactBytesLen=70 | ENCODE=OK | PAYLOAD=OK | REENCODE=FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_MALFORMED
exactKeys11=true | snapIsRecord=FALSE | manifestKeys=true | bindingKeys=true | digestMatch=true
```
Every structural check passed and the digest matched — but `snapshotFoundationValue(parsed)` returned HOSTILE.
ROOT CAUSE, on disk: **`packages/contracts/src/bounded-json-parser.ts:87` builds every parsed object with `Object.create(null)`**, and the shared `copyValue` refuses any non-array object whose prototype is not `Object.prototype`. So a payload this codec itself produced could never be re-admitted through the encoder's caller-facing path. This is why the sibling `readStoredFoundationAttempt` re-encodes `decoded.value` directly and never re-admits — it sidesteps the problem rather than solving it, which is fine for its shape but not for a codec that must re-validate every field on the way out.
FIX: a small `plainify()` that rebuilds the parsed value on `Object.prototype`. It is a PROTOTYPE ADAPTER, not a second canonical layer — it changes no key, no value and no ordering, and it runs only over bytes this module already produced. A null-prototype object arriving from a CALLER is still refused, because callers enter through the encoder and never through `plainify`; the hostile sweep's "a null-prototype record" case still passes, which is the check that this fix did not open a hole.

TWO TEST BUGS OF MY OWN, both fixed rather than worked around. `selectContext()` returns a `ContextSelectionResult`, not a selection — my step-4 variation arms cast the RESULT to `AdmittedContextSelection` and produced `TypeError: mandatory is not iterable` inside the real `renderContext`. Replaced the cast with a proper `otherManifest()` helper that checks `kind === "ADMITTED"` and throws on a refusal, so a fixture can never silently degrade. That helper now serves both the `manifest` sweep arm and the both-digests-move arm.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES worth QA's attention:
- `boundedInteger` uses `!Object.is(value, -0)`, which is the ONLY check that sees negative zero. Applied to `graphEpoch`, both journal limits, and every `exactBytes` entry.
- The outer digest is derived over the canonical BYTES of the ten bound fields plus this record's own version tag, via `encodeFoundationPayload`. Hashing bytes rather than a reference is what makes it depend on every nested value — `String(object)` is `"[object Object]"` for every distinct record, which is precisely drill (i).
- `deepFreeze` walks nested values; a shallow `Object.freeze` would leave `exactBytes`, `exclusions` and `optionalSelection` writable, and the step-3 test asserts all five levels.
- The decoder's order is: bounded decode -> plainify -> full re-admission -> RE-ENCODE and byte-compare -> only then return authority. NONCANONICAL is answered from the byte comparison, which is what separates "these bytes parse to a valid record" from "these bytes ARE the record".

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
COMPOSE THE EXISTING DAEMON CODEC HELPERS RATHER THAN WRITE A SECOND CANONICAL LAYER. `apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-codec.ts` (194 lines) already exports `exactKeys`, `snapshotFoundationValue`, `encodeFoundationPayload`, `decodeFoundationPayload`, `sameBytes`, `sha256Hex`, `isRecord` and `textOf` — the exact descriptor-safe and canonical-byte primitives this codec needs, in the same directory. A parallel implementation would drift from them, and the drift would live in durable bytes where it cannot be corrected after the fact.

THE OUTER DIGEST IS DERIVED, NEVER ACCEPTED. Considered letting the encoder validate a caller-supplied `recordDigest` and pass it through. Rejected: rail 2 forbids accepting a caller digest at all. Deriving it and refusing RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH on disagreement is strictly stronger, and it turns "the caller cannot supply authority" into a tested behaviour rather than a comment.

FIVE DISTINCT CODES, NOT ONE "BAD BYTES" CODE. MALFORMED, VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH, RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH and NONCANONICAL answer five different operator questions and must never stand in for each other. This mirrors the sibling `readStoredFoundationAttempt`, which keeps ABSENT / AMBIGUOUS / DRIFT separate for the same reason, and the `@moe/import` contract's own note that "the four DECODE codes are deliberately distinct rather than one bad-file code".

THE PER-FIELD DIGEST SWEEP IS THE CENTRAL TEST, not a nicety. DoD 4's mutation clause ("omitting an outer binding field") is only detectable if each of the ten outer fields is mutated INDIVIDUALLY and asserted to move the digest. A single "the digest changes when the record changes" assertion stays green while nine of ten fields are unbound.

planningNotes.risks:
1. NEGATIVE ZERO IS THE SUBTLE ONE, and DoD 4 names it deliberately. `JSON.stringify(-0)` is `"0"`, so a canonical encode/decode round-trip silently normalises it and every byte comparison still passes. Detect it with `Object.is(value, -0)` on `graphEpoch` and on every `exactBytes` entry; a `value === 0` check cannot see it, and neither can a digest comparison.
2. THE PER-FIELD SWEEP MUST BE PER FIELD. A lump assertion that "the digest changes when the record changes" passes while nine of the ten outer fields are unhashed. Assert the case count is exactly 10, and require drill (ii) to redden exactly one arm.
3. THE INNER DIGEST DOES NOT BIND OUTER FIELDS, and a plausible-looking shortcut is to reuse `manifest.digest` as the record's identity. That would let two records with different projectId or graphEpoch share an identity. The independence pair in step 4 exists to make that a red test.
4. THE `.js` BRIDGE MUST BE LF and rail 1 says so explicitly. It is invisible to typecheck and vitest, and a drill restore can silently reintroduce CRLF — re-verify the committed bytes after every restore.
5. DO NOT TOUCH packages/context. Rail 1 and rail 3 both forbid it, and rail 2 forbids copying its canonical digest. If `digestContextManifest` appears to need a change, that is a different task.
6. A refusal-only suite is blind to a wrong ACCEPTED value. The accepted control must run the REAL `selectContext` -> `renderContext` chain; a hand-forged manifest would prove only that the codec accepts what the test happens to build.
7. Reuse the sibling descriptor-safe helpers rather than writing new ones — a second `exactKeys` that admits an accessor while the original refuses it is a divergence living in durable bytes.
8. Mutation drills run in a shared worktree; snapshot hashes and restore by content, never `git checkout`.
